{
  "id": "I-0838",
  "title": null,
  "kind": "protection",
  "status": "open",
  "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 — the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.

WHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.

THE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT
- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` — reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.
- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` — takes the MOST important open representability item.
- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` — 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where "important" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.

CLAIMING — do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.
 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.
 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.
 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.
 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body "CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> — <one line on what discharging it buys>"`.
 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.

RANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap — rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.

YOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body "…"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts — propose to the human instead).

STANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.

WHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:
- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.
- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.
- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P → P`.
- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.

COMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",
  "comments": []
}

They include two board comments I created minutes ago, five AJC inbox items, and seven comment files across four other lanes' threads.\n\nAND THE MECHANISM THIS ITEM STILL DID NOT COVER, now filed as I-1271 and independently reproduced by ajc-p2 as I-1288: THE FRESH-INDEX DISCIPLINE BELOW IS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT. `read-tree HEAD` snapshots the WHOLE tree; `commit` writes the WHOLE index as a tree, not only the paths you added. So any path another lane advances between your read-tree and your commit is silently REVERTED by your commit -- as an M against a stale blob, with no D line, and with every pre-commit check passing because HEAD had not moved when you ran them. It happened to me this session on ajc-p1's galois row (3bf50581e7), restored byte-identical in 83abf6dc00.\n\nSO THE COMPLETE PROCEDURE, both halves required:\n 1. BEFORE: fresh index file (rm -f), read-tree HEAD, add ONLY explicit paths, confirm the staged stat lists only those paths, commit -- all with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999).\n 2. AFTER, and this is the half that catches the race: `diff HEAD~1 HEAD --stat` and READ EVERY PATH. A path you did not add means you reverted it; restore from disk, which still holds their version. Also read the DELETION COUNT rather than the exit code.\nI ran step 2 on all ten of my commits this session; it caught the one clobber within a minute.\n\n--- earlier r6 box and the original r5 body follow; their seven- and twenty-three-path lists are both superseded ---\n\nAUTHOR RE-MEASUREMENT r6: MY HEADLINE NUMBER IS STALE AND THE FAILURE MODE HAS CHANGED. They are MODIFICATIONS to stale blobs, which produce NO D line. A lane following this item's own advice (\"confirm the staged stat lists ONLY your paths\") is protected; a lane that merely greps `^D` is NOT.\n\nSO, discipline unchanged, with the reading rule now explicit: fresh index file (rm -f, read-tree HEAD, add explicit paths, confirm the stat lists only those paths, commit), all four steps with GIT_INDEX_FILE pointed at that file. Never copy the shared index; never read-tree HEAD into it (I-0999). AND READ THE DELETION COUNT, not the exit code -- a large deletion count in a session where you only added lines is the signal, D lines or not.\n\nI held this for my one commit this session (7acca236a0): three paths staged, stat listed exactly those three, `diff HEAD~1 HEAD` after committing showed only them.\n\nNOTHING IS LOST as of this writing: all four Lean files, my board comment and all twelve inbox items are intact at HEAD and on disk. Still a warning about the next plain commit, not a damage report.\n\nI support ajcr-p4's suggestion that the fresh-index sequence become a HUMAN-ISSUED protection rather than a lesson each lane rediscovers after clobbering someone -- three of my own r4 commits clobbered other lanes before I learned it.\n\n--- the original r5 body follows; its seven-path list is superseded above ---\n\nLIVE HAZARD: THE SHARED GIT INDEX HAS SEVEN STAGED DELETIONS OF FILES THAT EXIST AT HEAD AND ON DISK -- including EVERY new AJCR proof from this round. Do NOT commit from the shared index. Confirms and extends ajcr-p1's I-1220, whose list was shorter.\n\nRE-MEASURED by review-ajcr r5, independently. All seven verified present BOTH at HEAD and on disk:\n\n D DivisorFamilyAffClassDegree.lean   (hdegAff DISCHARGED -- p1, this round)\n D Pic0AtlasFromDivRepAff.lean        (the WIDENED Sigma-chart -- p1, this round)\n D Pic0ChartBotRefute.lean            (the V=bot refutation -- p4, this round)\n D Pic0ChartLocusH0One.lean           (p2's locus work, this round)\n D roadmap items .../c9-chartlocus.chart-u-aff.yaml  (p3's new row)\n D roadmap comments AJCR.w4-rep/C-0011.md            (my re-ranking)\n D roadmap comments .../abel-widened/C-0003.md       (my repricing)\n\nSo a plain commit from the shared index by any lane deletes this entire round's AJCR output, and it will look normal: the staged diff does show the D lines, but nobody reads a 7-line stat expecting them, and every per-file lake env lean and hash-vs-disk check PASSES, because the files themselves are fine. THE RULE, for any session on the DD-R certificate lane or its consumers:

 1. DO NOT BUILD THE GL_2(k) ACTION ON P1. Roadmap leaf AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.p1-aut stays pending and DEPRIORITISED — not rejected (R1 may still accelerate the large-field case one day), but no session spends time on it, and no consumer may be written against it.  2. The widening target: FinCoverData s pieces become arbitrary affine opens rather than basic opens of a FIXED PAIR of pinned P1 charts. Justification to use, not to re-derive: supp D is finite over R, hence lies in a single affine open of C x_k Spec R (Stacks 0B8B); spec-dd-r.md ADDENDUM 4 carries the argument.

 3. THE CHART-WISE PARTITIONS OF UNITY ARE WHAT HAS TO GO. Per-piece swallow-or-miss needs only openness (DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean uses only openness); it is the partitions that upgrade inside one piece to inside one chart. Removing them will break consumers — repair the consumers deliberately, and do not smuggle the old typing back in by typing pieces INTO the charts (DivisorFamily.lean h0/h1/pieces is exactly the pattern that made the previous cheaper option vacuous).

 4. TWO OBLIGATIONS THE WIDENING RELOCATES RATHER THAN REMOVES, both to be discharged explicitly and neither to be hidden inside a LocalEquations: (i) fibrewise-finite support, which must come from the seed s own degree data; (ii) whatever the old fixed-pair confinement was silently supplying to the certificate clauses.

 5. THE STANDING NEGATIVE RESULTS REMAIN BINDING, all established by predecessor sessions and adversarially checked. Chart-avoid is NO. The counterexample is FIELD-INDEPENDENT, so enlarging the field is not an escape. And the sharp form to quote: NO repair that keeps the pieces inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR of points of P1 can work. The joint-cover variant is refuted (leaf ...joint-cover, rejected) — do not retry it.

WHY R2 AND NOT A FIELD-SIZE HYPOTHESIS: archon-protected.yaml freezes the arbitrary-field statement, so |P1(k)| >= n+2 would answer a different question. R2 is the only field-uniform fix. The sharpness result (leaf ...field-size, done) stands and needs no further human input.

10.2 Formal proof strategy
5.    Twist by a sufficiently positive base-field line bundle until H^1 vanishes and H^0 is nonzero.
6.    If h^0 is greater than one, choose a k-rational point at which a nonzero section does not vanish.
7.    Subtract that point and use the exact sequence to lower h^0 by one while preserving H^1 = 0.
8.    Repeat until h^0 = 1.

        (K : Type*) [Field K] [Algebra k K]

1. Executive summary
The project has made real progress, especially in widened divisor-family infrastructure, rank calculations,
and finite-Galois descent machinery. However, the current code growth does not yet correspond to
comparable movement toward the final Picard representability theorem. The central reason is architectural:
large divisor degree gives coverage but destroys Abel-map injectivity, while genus degree gives rank-one
uniqueness but is harder to cover over an arbitrary base field.

The recommended route is therefore AJCR-first and follows the curve-specialized classical construction:
build a rank-one Picard open over a separably closed field, represent it by an open inside the degree-g
divisor scheme, cover the Picard functor by translations of this open, then descend the resulting Pic^0
through finite Galois descent. AJC should be used as the shared descent engine and long-term infrastructure
project rather than as a second independent Picard proof.

  Primary decision
  The next endpoint-critical theorem is the family-level natural isomorphism between the rank-one open
  inside Div^g and the rank-one open inside the Picard functor. Parameter decoupling remains useful
  infrastructure, but it is no longer the main Picard endpoint lane.

2. The three principal issues
2.1 Coverage degree and injectivity degree are incompatible
On a genus-g curve, a nonspecial divisor of degree n has h^0 = n + 1 - g. At a sufficiently large admissible
degree, coverage is available, but h^0 is greater than 1 in positive genus. The Abel map then has positive-
dimensional linear-system fibres and cannot directly be the monomorphism or open immersion required by
the existing Picard chart seam.

At degree n = g, the same rank formula gives h^0 = 1 on the nonspecial locus, so uniqueness and an open-
immersion chart become possible. However, the required degree-g translation data need not exist over an
arbitrary base field. The project has therefore been attempting to make two different parameter regimes
solve one seam.

    Parameter regime                   What it gives                       What fails

    n=g                                Rank-one fibres; potential open     Pointwise coverage over the original
                                       immersion                           base field

    n = admissible > g                 Uniform coverage and large-degree   Injectivity; the Abel fibres have h^0 >
                                       control                             1




2.2 Lean interfaces are hiding mathematical misalignment
Several classifier layers use one symbol for distinct semantic roles: curve genus, divisor degree, and window
parameters. Equivalent geometric objects are also represented by different Lean expressions, causing
expensive definitional-equality and typeclass-search failures. Weak existential witnesses and source/test-
locus mismatches have allowed locally true lemmas to accumulate without closing the intended producer.

      Hard-coded diagonal relation n = g in classifier and RepresentableBy layers.
      Repeated transports between relCurve-style and explicit base-change expressions.
      Duplicate diagonal and generalized proofs surviving in parallel.
      Fieldwise uniqueness results used where the consumer needs a natural inverse on arbitrary test
       schemes.
      Compatibility wrappers that move hypotheses but do not create the missing geometric map.

2.3 The final theorem chain is not yet closed
The repository contains many strong components, but the final path is still discontinuous. The missing
central theorem is not another rank or coverage lemma; it is a family-level identification of the correct
divisor open with the correct Picard open, followed by a complete descent theorem returning both the
descended scheme and its RepresentableBy certificate.

---
name: horizon-start
description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
---

Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
ago, and their report was written for you.

This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
tenth of the session.

## The four signals

```bash
ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
```

The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
like:

```
0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
0003-system
0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
```

For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:

- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
  single most informative bit on disk.
- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
  four minutes ago or last week.

## Which situation am I in?

Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.

**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.

**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
ledger.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
tried and rejected.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
stand before proposing work.

One caveat about round numbers. `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is 0-based and reliable
for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
the run's original plan.)

## Then, before you start

- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.
- **The inbox is the cross-session thread** — read what past sessions left for
  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
  `horizon-inbox`.

Then stop orienting and start working. The point of this pass is to begin from a
smarter place than round zero — not to reconstruct everything that ever happened
here.

---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

    41	    (hx : e.base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint K) = x) :
    42	    X.left.residueDeg K x = 1 := by
    43	  letI : Algebra K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x) := stalkAlgebra X.hom x
    44	  have h := bijective_algebraMap_residueField_of_section X he hx
    45	  have hmap :
    46	      algebraMap K (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)) =
    47	        X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x := by
    48	    ext c
    49	    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_apply K (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)
    50	      (IsLocalRing.ResidueField (X.left.presheaf.stalk x)),
    51	      IsLocalRing.ResidueField.algebraMap_eq, Scheme.residueOverAlgebraMap,
    52	      algebraMap_overStalkAlgebra]
    53	    simp [stalkStructureHom, Scheme.overAlgebraMap]
    54	    rfl
    55	  letI : Algebra K (X.left.residueField x) :=
    56	    (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x).toAlgebra
    57	  unfold Scheme.residueDeg
    58	  change Module.finrank K (X.left.residueField x) = 1
    59	  apply Module.finrank_of_bijective_algebraMap
    60	  change Function.Bijective (X.left.residueOverAlgebraMap K x)
    61	  rw [← hmap]
    62	  exact h
    63	
    64	/-! ## The base-changed rational point is such a section -/
    65	
    66	theorem residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange
    67	    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    68	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    69	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    70	    (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
    71	    (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))) :
    72	    ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).residueDeg L
    73	      ((Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L)) = 1 := by
    74	  apply residueDeg_one_of_section
    75	    (X := Over.mk (snd C (overSpec k L)).left)
    76	    (e := Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp)
    77	  · exact Over.rationalPointBaseChange_snd C L p hp
    78	  · rfl
    79	
    80	/-! ## Image-set packaging -/
    81	
    82	theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChange_image
    83	    {k : Type u} [Field k]
    84	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    85	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    86	    (P : Set (relCurve C L))
    87	    (hP : ∀ x ∈ P, ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
    88	      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
    89	      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x) :
    90	    ∀ x ∈ P, (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
    91	  intro x hx
    92	  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hP x hx
    93	  rw [← hpx]
    94	  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp
    95	
    96	/-! ## The dense point image used by the drop oracle -/
    97	
    98	/-- The points obtained by base-changing actual `k`-rational sections of `C` to `L`.
    99	
   100	The section certificate is retained in the membership predicate, so later consumers can recover
   101	the base point and its exact residue-degree proof.  This is deliberately an image set, rather
   102	than an existential carrier unrelated to the chosen curve and extension. -/
   103	def rationalPointBaseChangeImage
   104	    {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   105	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] : Set (relCurve C L) :=
   106	  {x | ∃ (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ C.left)
   107	      (hp : p ≫ C.hom = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k))),
   108	      (Over.rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp).base
   109	        (IsLocalRing.closedPoint L) = x}
   110	
   111	/-- Base-changed `k`-rational points are dense over a separably closed base. -/
   112	theorem dense_rationalPointBaseChangeImage
   113	    {k : Type u} [Field k] [IsSepClosed k]
   114	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   115	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
   116	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsIntegral C.left]
   117	    (U : (relCurve C L).Opens)
   118	    (hU : (U : Set (relCurve C L)).Nonempty) :
   119	    (rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L ∩ U).Nonempty := by
   120	  obtain ⟨p, hp, hmem⟩ := Over.dense_baseChange_rationalPoints C L U hU
   121	  exact ⟨_, ⟨⟨p, hp, rfl⟩, hmem⟩⟩
   122	
   123	/-- Every point in the dense image has residue degree one, by its retained section certificate. -/
   124	theorem residueDeg_one_of_mem_rationalPointBaseChangeImage'
   125	    {k : Type u} [Field k]
   126	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   127	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   128	    ∀ x ∈ rationalPointBaseChangeImage C L,
   129	      (relCurve C L).residueDeg L x = 1 := by
   130	  intro x hx
   131	  obtain ⟨p, hp, hpx⟩ := hx
   132	  rw [← hpx]
   133	  exact residueDeg_one_of_rationalPointBaseChange C L p hp
   134

    11	/-!
    12	# The consumed local divisor package for the rank-one route
    13	
    14	This module is the first divisor consumer of PicRankOneLocalPresentation.  The projective
    15	rank-one H0 module supplies a basic open and a section which is nonzero on every residue fibre
    16	there.  The datum-side section construction then gives regular local equations, and the widened
    17	effectivity engine packages those equations as a DivFamZarAff of degree genus C.
    18	
    19	The package is deliberately local and presentation-tied.  It does not define the canonical
    20	family-level divisorOfRankOne, identify the equations with the native zero locus, or assert
    21	that the rank-one locus is represented by an open subscheme.  Those remain the next contracts.
    22	-/
    23	
    24	set_option autoImplicit false
    25	
    26	universe u
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits TopologicalSpace Opposite MonoidalCategory
    29	  CartesianMonoidalCategory
    30	open scoped TensorProduct
    31	
    32	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    33	
    34	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    35	attribute [local instance 10000] relCurve.instOver

    39	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

    42	variable {lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)}

    45	
    46	/- The degree theorem needs the base-change geometric package under the local relCurve instance,
    47	   which has lower priority in the general curve API. -/

    49	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    50	    (relCurve C L).Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
    51	  instOverBaseChange C L
    52	
    53	noncomputable local instance rankOneLocalDivisorSmooth
    54	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    55	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
    56	  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L

    59	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
    60	    IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=
    61	  instIsIntegralBaseChange C L

    75	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=

    78	/-! ## Regularity and degree of the local equations -/
    79	
    80	/-- The local equations cut from the tied datum section remain regular after every field-valued
    81	coefficient extension.  This is the regularity input consumed by the widened effectivity
    82	engine, derived from the same fibrewise nonvanishing hypothesis used in the construction. -/
    83	theorem baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations_fibrewiseRegular
    84	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
    85	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
    86	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
    87	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
    88	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
    89	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
    90	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
    91	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
    92	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    93	    [Algebra (Localization.Away f) L]
    94	    [IsScalarTower k (Localization.Away f) L]
    95	    (z : relCurve C L) :
    96	    ((relCurve C L).presheaf.germ
    97	      (((P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations f y hy).cover.pullback
    98	        (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away f) L)).opens z) z
    99	      (((P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations f y hy).cover.pullback
   100	        (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away f) L)).mem_opens z)).hom
   101	      (Scheme.LocalEquations.pullbackEqn
   102	        (relCurveMap C (Localization.Away f) L)
   103	        (P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations f y hy) z) ∈
   104	      nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C L).presheaf.stalk z) := by
   105	  let B := Localization.Away f
   106	  let D := P.datum.baseChange B
   107	  let s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤) :=
   108	    P.datumSectionBaseChange B y
   109	  have hsec : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
   110	      D.sectionsMapTop q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   111	        (P.datumSectionBaseChange B y) ≠ 0 :=
   112	    fun q => P.sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero f y hy q
   113	  have hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (q : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
   114	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   115	    fun j q => D.injective_rTensor_component_of_sectionsMapTop_ne_zero
   116	      s q (hsec q) j
   117	  unfold baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange
   118	  exact D.germ_self_pullbackEqn_sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
   119	    s hfib L z

   121	/-- The local equations have the genus class degree after every field-valued extension.  The
   122	calculation uses the datum class law and datum_classDeg_baseChange, so the degree is tied to
   123	the presentation rather than supplied as an unrelated witness. -/
   124	theorem baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations_classDeg
   125	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   126	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   127	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)

   225	/-- The Abel value of the local divisor is the restriction of the input Picard datum.  This is
   226	the immediate consumer which keeps the widened divisor tied to the chosen presentation. -/
   227	theorem baseOpenRankOneDivisor_abelAff
   228	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   229	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   230	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   231	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   232	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   233	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   234	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   235	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
   236	    abelDivAffPlus C (Localization.Away f) (P.baseOpenRankOneDivisor f y hy) =
   237	      PicEtAff.mapAlg C ((Algebra.ofId P.cover.Carrier (Localization.Away f)).restrictScalars k)
   238	        (PicEtAff.mapAlg C ((Algebra.ofId A P.cover.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
   239	          (picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1)) := by
   240	  let B := Localization.Away f
   241	  let iota : A →ₐ[k] P.cover.Carrier :=
   242	    (Algebra.ofId A P.cover.Carrier).restrictScalars k
   243	  let psi : P.cover.Carrier →ₐ[k] B :=
   244	    (Algebra.ofId P.cover.Carrier B).restrictScalars k
   245	  let F := P.baseOpenRankOneDivisor f y hy
   246	  have hFclass : F.picClass = (P.datum.baseChange B).cechPicClass :=
   247	    P.baseOpenRankOneDivisor_picClass f y hy
   248	  have hrel : (relPicMk C (overSpec k B)) F.picClass =
   249	      relPicAlgMap C psi (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)) := by
   250	    rw [hFclass, P.datum_class, relPicAlgMap_mk]
   251	    have hcurve : Over.Hom.left (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap psi) =
   252	        relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B := by
   253	      refine congrArg (fun f : overSpec k B ⟶ overSpec k P.cover.Carrier => (C ◁ f).left) ?_
   254	      exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl
   255	    rw [P.datum.cechPicClass_baseChange B, hcurve]
   256	    rfl
   257	  calc
   258	    abelDivAffPlus C B F = PicEtAff.unit C B ((relPicMk C (overSpec k B)) F.picClass) := rfl
   259	    _ = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicAlgMap C psi
   260	      (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))) := by rw [hrel]
   261	    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C psi
   262	      (PicEtAff.unit C P.cover.Carrier
   263	        (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))) := by
   264	      rw [PicEtAff.mapAlg_unit]
   265	    _ = PicEtAff.mapAlg C psi (PicEtAff.mapAlg C iota (picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1)) := by
   266	      congr 1
   267	      rw [← P.represents, PicEtAff.mapAlg_mk_eq_unit_self]

   272	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)

   275	    ∃ f : P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧

     9	/-!
    10	# DAT-B B-1 — the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop to `h⁰ = 1`
    11	
    12	The coverage-side normalization of the DAT-B worksheet (`informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md`
    13	§1.4, COV-2): on the curve bundle `Y` over a field `K` (the fibre field of the coverage
    14	argument), given an **admissible point oracle** `P` — a set of closed `K`-rational points
    15	(`residueDeg = 1`) meeting every nonempty open — and a divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with
    16	`H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`, there is an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with
    17	
    18	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`
    19	  (`exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one`, the keystone).
    20	
    21	The pointwise coverage theorem (B-5, worksheet §1.2 step 5) consumes this with
    22	`P :=` the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points supplied by the density oracle of B-2
    23	(`Curve/SepPointsDense.lean`); the oracle parametrization decouples the density
    24	discharge from the pure Riemann–Roch drop.
    25	
    26	## Route (worksheet §1.4, per step for the current `W'` with `h¹ = 0`, `deg = g + e'`)
    27	
    28	* **The bad locus is small** (`exists_admissible_nonbase_point`): `H⁰(𝒪(W'))` is nonzero
    29	  (rank anchor `h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one`), its base divisor
    30	  (`Scheme.baseDivisor`, the DD-F kit) has finite support consisting of closed points, so
    31	  the non-base locus contains a nonempty open (complement of a finite closed set in the
    32	  irreducible curve — it contains the generic point) and the oracle supplies an admissible
    33	  point there; the base-divisor achiever (`exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) turns
    34	  "outside the support" into an exact-order section.
    35	* **Exact drop at a rational non-base point** (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`):
    36	  `h⁰(𝒪(W' − x)) ≤ h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1` — sections of `W' − x` are sections of `W'`, a *proper*
    37	  submodule since the non-base section violates the deeper pole bound at `x`
    38	  (`Submodule.finrank_lt_finrank_of_lt` through the `h⁰` bridge
    39	  `finrank_divisorSections_top`) — while the χ-ledger (`chi_divisorSheaf`) with
    40	  `residueDeg x = 1` and `h¹(𝒪(W')) = 0` gives `χ(𝒪(W' − x)) = h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1`; equality
    41	  forces BOTH `h⁰(𝒪(W' − x)) = h⁰(𝒪(W')) − 1` AND `h¹(𝒪(W' − x)) = 0` — the induction
    42	  invariant.
    43	* **Terminate at `e' = 0`**: `h⁰ = 1` by the rank anchor at `deg = g`, `χ(𝒪) = 1 − g`.
    44	
    45	The strict-drop precedents `h0_normalization_sub_single_lt` (`PFib.lean`) and
    46	`h0_window_sub_single_lt` (`CarveDegreePinch.lean`) are window-specific mirrors of the
    47	drop step (worksheet risk 3 mitigation); their `deg_single`/`coeffAt` bookkeeping is
    48	imitated, not consumed.  Pure field level — no scheme beyond the fibre curve appears
    49	(the DD-F discipline).  The genus enters only through `hχ : χ(𝒪_Y) = 1 − g`; the
    50	worksheet's standing `h⁰(𝒪_Y) = 1` is not needed by this brick and is not threaded.
    51	-/
    52	
    53	set_option autoImplicit false
    54	
    55	universe u
    56	
    57	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    58	
    59	attribute [local instance] AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.functionFieldOverModule
    60	  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.overModule
    61	
    62	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    63	
    64	open Scheme
    65	
    66	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
    67	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    68	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    69	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    70	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    71	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    72	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    73	
    74	/-! ## The bad locus is small: an admissible non-base point -/
    75	
    76	omit [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    77	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)] in
    78	/-- **An admissible non-base point** (worksheet §1.4 bullet 1): if `H⁰(𝒪(W))` is nonzero
    79	and `P` is dense (meets every nonempty open) and consists of closed points, then some
    80	`x ∈ P` is *not* a base point of the system: some nonzero section `f ∈ H⁰(𝒪(W))` has
    81	exact order at `x`, `(W + div f)ₓ = 0`.  The base locus is contained in the support of
    82	the base divisor `bd(H⁰(𝒪(W)))` — a finite set of closed points, whose complement is a
    83	nonempty open (it contains the generic point); the base-divisor achiever
    84	(`Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt`) realizes the vanishing base multiplicity
    85	outside the support. -/
    86	theorem exists_admissible_nonbase_point (P : Set Y)
    87	    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
    88	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint Y)
    89	    (W : Y.CurveDivisor) (hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W)) :
    90	    ∃ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (_ : x ∈ P) (f : Y.functionField)
    91	      (_ : f ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤) (hf : f ≠ 0),
    92	      coeffAt hx (W + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
    93	        = 0 := by
    94	  classical
    95	  set T : Submodule K Y.functionField := divisorSections K W ⊤ with hT
    96	  have hTne : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0 := by
    97	    refine Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot (fun hbot => ?_)
    98	    have hfr : Module.finrank K ↥T = Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) :=
    99	      finrank_divisorSections_top K W
   100	    rw [hbot, finrank_bot] at hfr
   101	    omega
   102	  set B : Y.CurveDivisor := Scheme.baseDivisor K T W hTne with hB
   103	  -- the support of the base divisor is a finite set of closed points
   104	  have hclosed : IsClosed (⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y)) :=
   105	    isClosed_biUnion_finset (fun p _ =>
   106	      isClosed_singleton_of_ne_genericPoint (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) p.2)
   107	  set U : Y.Opens :=
   108	    ⟨(⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y))ᶜ, hclosed.isOpen_compl⟩ with hU
   109	  have hUne : (U : Set Y).Nonempty := by
   110	    refine ⟨genericPoint Y, fun hmem => ?_⟩
   111	    obtain ⟨p, _, hp⟩ := Set.mem_iUnion₂.mp hmem
   112	    exact p.2 (Set.mem_singleton_iff.mp hp).symm
   113	  obtain ⟨x, hxP, hxU⟩ := hdense U hUne
   114	  have hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y := hPcl x hxP
   115	  -- outside the support the base multiplicity vanishes
   116	  have hxc : x ∉ ⋃ p ∈ (toFinsupp B).support, ({p.1} : Set Y) := hxU
   117	  have hxB : coeffAt hx B = 0 := by
   118	    by_contra hne
   119	    exact hxc (Set.mem_iUnion₂.mpr
   120	      ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, Finsupp.mem_support_iff.mpr hne, rfl⟩)
   121	  have hBat : (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T W ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ) = 0 := by
   122	    rw [← Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor K hTne hx]
   123	    exact hxB
   124	  -- the achiever realizes the vanishing base multiplicity
   125	  obtain ⟨f, hfT, hf, hach⟩ :=
   126	    Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt K (le_refl T) hTne hx
   127	  exact ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfT, hf, hach.trans hBat⟩
   128	
   129	/-! ## The exact drop at a rational non-base point -/
   130	
   131	/-- **The exact drop** (worksheet §1.4 bullet 2): at a closed `K`-rational point `x`
   132	(`residueDeg x = 1`) that is not a base point of `H⁰(𝒪(W))` — witnessed by a nonzero
   133	section `f` of exact order at `x` — and under `H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`,
   134	
   135	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − x)) + 1 = h⁰(𝒪(W))`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − x)) = 0`.
   136	
   137	`≤`: sections of `W − x` are sections of `W` vanishing one order deeper at `x`, a proper
   138	subspace since `f` violates the deeper bound — one linear condition as `residueDeg x = 1`.
   139	`≥`: the χ-ledger gives `χ(𝒪(W − x)) = χ(𝒪(W)) − 1 = h⁰(𝒪(W)) − 1` and `h¹ ≥ 0`.
   140	Equality forces both conclusions — the induction invariant of the greedy drop. -/
   141	theorem h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase (W : Y.CurveDivisor)
   142	    (h1W : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1))
   143	    {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (hdx : Y.residueDeg K x = 1)
   144	    {f : Y.functionField} (hfW : f ∈ divisorSections K W ⊤) (hf : f ≠ 0)
   145	    (hnb : coeffAt hx (W + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
   146	      = 0) :
   147	    Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) + 1
   148	        = Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) ∧
   149	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)) 1) := by
   150	  -- sections of `W − x` sit inside sections of `W` …

   153	    refine divisorSections_mono K ?_ ⊤
   154	    refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun y hy => ?_)
   155	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub]
   156	    by_cases hyx : y = x
   157	    · subst hyx
   158	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self]
   159	      omega
   160	    · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx]
   161	      omega
   162	  -- … properly: the exact-order section violates the deeper bound at `x`
   163	  have hfnot : f ∉ divisorSections K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) ⊤ := by
   164	    intro hmem
   165	    have h0le := (mem_divisorSections_top_iff K hf).mp hmem
   166	    have hcoeff := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp h0le x hx
   167	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub,
   168	      CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self] at hcoeff
   169	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at hnb

   172	      ≠ divisorSections K W ⊤ := by
   173	    intro heq
   174	    rw [← heq] at hfW

   182	  have hchiWx := chi_divisorSheaf K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   183	  have hdegsub : CurveDivisor.deg K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   184	      = CurveDivisor.deg K W - 1 := by

   198	/-! ## The keystone: the greedy drop to `h⁰ = 1` -/
   199	
   200	/-- **COV-2, the oracle-parametrized greedy `h⁰`-drop** (★ B-1 keystone, worksheet §1.4):
   201	on the curve bundle `Y` over the field `K` with `χ(𝒪_Y) = 1 − g`, let `P` be an
   202	admissible point oracle — closed points, `K`-rational (`residueDeg = 1`), dense (meeting
   203	every nonempty open).  Then every divisor `W` of degree `g + e` with `H¹(𝒪(W)) = 0`
   204	admits an effective divisor `Σ` of degree `e` supported in `P` with
   205	
   206	  `h⁰(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 1`  and  `H¹(𝒪(W − Σ)) = 0`.
   207	
   208	Induction on `e`: at each step the rank anchor gives `h⁰ = e' + 1 ≥ 1`, the oracle
   209	supplies a rational non-base point (`exists_admissible_nonbase_point`), and the exact
   210	drop (`h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase`) preserves the invariant `h¹ = 0` while
   211	lowering the degree budget by one.  The pointwise coverage theorem (B-5) instantiates
   212	`P` with the base-changed `C(K_s)`-points of B-2. -/
   213	theorem exists_effective_sub_h0_eq_one (g : ℕ)
   214	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
   215	    (P : Set Y)
   216	    (hdense : ∀ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y).Nonempty → (P ∩ U).Nonempty)
   217	    (hPcl : ∀ x ∈ P, x ≠ genericPoint Y)
   218	    (hPdeg : ∀ x ∈ P, Y.residueDeg K x = 1)
   219	    (W : Y.CurveDivisor) (e : ℕ)
   220	    (hdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) + e)
   221	    (h1 : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1)) :
   222	    ∃ S : Y.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   223	      (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   224	      Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
   225	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) := by
   226	  suffices H : ∀ (e : ℕ) (W : Y.CurveDivisor),
   227	      CurveDivisor.deg K W = (g : ℤ) + e →
   228	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1) →
   229	      ∃ S : Y.CurveDivisor, 0 ≤ S ∧ CurveDivisor.deg K S = (e : ℤ) ∧
   230	        (∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), coeffAt hx S ≠ 0 → x ∈ P) ∧
   231	        Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) = 1 ∧
   232	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (W - S)) 1) from
   233	    H e W hdeg h1
   234	  intro e
   235	  induction e with
   236	  | zero =>
   237	    intro W hdeg h1
   238	    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
   239	    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
   240	    refine ⟨0, le_refl 0, by rw [CurveDivisor.deg_zero, Nat.cast_zero], ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   241	    · intro x hx hne
   242	      exact (hne (CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero hx)).elim
   243	    · rw [sub_zero]
   244	      push_cast at hanchor
   245	      omega
   246	    · rw [sub_zero]
   247	      exact h1
   248	  | succ e ih =>
   249	    intro W hdeg h1
   250	    -- `h⁰(𝒪(W)) = e + 2 > 0` by the rank anchor
   251	    have hanchor := h0_eq_deg_add_chi_of_subsingleton_hModule_one (K := K) W h1
   252	    rw [hχ, hdeg] at hanchor
   253	    have hpos : 0 < Sheaf.h0 (Y.divisorSheaf K W) := by
   254	      push_cast at hanchor
   255	      omega
   256	    -- an admissible non-base point and the exact drop there
   257	    obtain ⟨x, hx, hxP, f, hfW, hf, hnb⟩ :=
   258	      exists_admissible_nonbase_point P hdense hPcl W hpos
   259	    obtain ⟨hdrop, h1'⟩ :=
   260	      h0_sub_single_of_rational_nonbase W h1 hx (hPdeg x hxP) hfW hf hnb
   261	    have hdeg' : CurveDivisor.deg K (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) = (g : ℤ) + e := by
   262	      rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' K, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1,
   263	        hPdeg x hxP, Nat.cast_one, mul_one, hdeg]
   264	      push_cast
   265	      ring
   266	    obtain ⟨S', hS'0, hS'deg, hS'P, hS'h0, hS'h1⟩ :=
   267	      ih (W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1) hdeg' h1'
   268	    have hsplit : W - (S' + CurveDivisor.single hx 1)
   269	        = W - CurveDivisor.single hx 1 - S' := by
   270	      abel
   271	    refine ⟨S' + CurveDivisor.single hx 1, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
   272	    · -- effectivity
   273	      refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun y hy => ?_)
   274	      have h0S' := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp hS'0 y hy
   275	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at h0S'
   276	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add]
   277	      by_cases hyx : y = x
   278	      · subst hyx
   279	        rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_self]
   280	        omega
   281	      · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx]
   282	        omega
   283	    · -- degree
   284	      rw [CurveDivisor.deg_add, hS'deg, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_single' K hx 1,
   285	        hPdeg x hxP, Nat.cast_one, mul_one]
   286	      push_cast
   287	      ring
   288	    · -- support in `P`
   289	      intro y hy hne
   290	      rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at hne
   291	      by_cases hyx : y = x
   292	      · subst hyx
   293	        exact hxP
   294	      · rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_single_of_ne hx hy hyx, add_zero] at hne
   295	        exact hS'P y hy hne
   296	    · rw [hsplit]
   297	      exact hS'h0
   298	    · rw [hsplit]
   299	      exact hS'h1

     9	/-!
    10	# COVERAGE NEEDS NO DROP, NO ORACLE, AND NO STEP 6
    11	
    12	A retraction of this lane's own account of B-5, and it removes a residue rather than adding one.
    13	
    14	`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageTest.lean`'s DEFECT section establishes — correctly — that the
    15	`w4-datb` §1.2 argument as written runs the greedy drop at `Z := 0` and feeds the drop's
    16	**output** `Σ` back as the chart index's `Z`, so that the two stages carry different `Z`, and
    17	that this feedback ("step 6") is not discharged anywhere.  It records step 6 as one of B-5's
    18	open residues.
    19	
    20	**Step 6 is not a residue, because coverage does not need the drop at all.**
    21	
    22	## Why: read what `chartLocus` actually asks for
    23	
    24	`IsSplitWitness` (`Pic0ChartLocus.lean:151`) — and its own docstring says this at length, under
    25	"A convention this predicate INHERITS" — asks for a divisor `W` in the presenting class with
    26	`Subsingleton H¹(𝒪(W))`, and asks for **neither `0 ≤ W` nor `deg W = g`**.  Effectivity and the
    27	degree normalisation are what the *chart map's injectivity* needs (GAP-2, `h⁰ = 1`), not what
    28	*membership of the locus* needs.
    29	
    30	The drop (`RiemannRoch/CoverageDrop.lean`) exists to manufacture exactly those two extra
    31	properties: it takes a degree-`g+e` witness with `h¹ = 0` and produces an effective `S` with
    32	`h⁰(W₀ − S) = 1`.  For membership, that work is thrown away — `mem_chartLocus_of_drop` returns
    33	the `IsSplitWitness` half from `hW₀`/`h1` alone, and its own proof shows this: the split witness
    34	comes from `isSplitWitness_of_witness_twistClass C μ m Z M₀ hM₀ W₀ hW₀ h1`, in which the drop,
    35	the oracle `P`, `hdense`, `hPcl`, `hPdeg`, `g`, `e`, `hχ` and `hdeg` **do not appear**.
    36	
    37	So the feedback of step 6 was an artefact of routing coverage through the drop.  Cut the drop
    38	and there is one `Z` again — the chart index's — and nothing to feed back.
    39	
    40	## What coverage then needs, in full
    41	
    42	Exactly one input beyond the landed splitting: a divisor of the twisted fibre class over the
    43	splitting field with vanishing `H¹`.  That is DAT-0a at the fibre field, and it is genuinely
    44	per-fibre (I-0204, `w4-datb` §0.2.2): no uniform `m₀` exists, so the exponent `m` must be chosen
    45	against `L`'s own threshold `b_L`.
    46	
    47	**CORRECTED 2026-07-30 in its second sentence** (`Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageThreshold.lean`,
    48	inbox `I-1329`).  The *threshold* is not per-fibre.  I-0204 says the per-field ledger
    49	**constants** do not transport — true — but the vanishing bound induced at `L` is base-field
    50	data: `subsingleton_hModule_one_of_witness` (`RiemannRoch/WindowFieldTransport.lean:87`) is
    51	π-free, `windowN C L hπ g` is a witness at every `L`, and `deg_windowN = M·δ` with
    52	`windowM_choice`/`windowδ` computed at `k`.  So `M·δ + g` is **one threshold for every
    53	splitting field**.
    54	
    55	**TWO CORRECTIONS TO THAT CORRECTION, both the same day** (audit + author reproduction, inbox
    56	`I-1349`/`I-1350`), so read the paragraph above only for its central point:
    57	
    58	* the sentence that stood here — "DAT-0a itself cannot be instantiated at `L`, there is no
    59	  `relCurve C L ⟶ P1 L` in this tree" — is **FALSE**.  `exists_isFinite_isDominant_toP1`
    60	  (`Curve/MapToP1.lean:126`) produces one for `baseChangeBundle C L` via the instances in
    61	  `Curve/BaseChangeInstances.lean`, so DAT-0a *is* available at `L`;
    62	* the uniform threshold is **not new Lean** either: `subsingleton_h1_of_windowA_le_deg`
    63	  (`Picard/DivSchemeSeedUnivFibre.lean:259`, landed 2026-07-19) is the same fact at a *smaller*
    64	  bound (`windowA_choice ≤ windowM_choice`).  Cite that, not
    65	  `subsingleton_h1_of_ledger_bound`.
    66	
    67	What survives is only the correction to the *"per-fibre"* reading itself, which was the point.
    68	Also unaffected: the retraction below, `hb_forces_h0_eq_one`, and the whole `b = g` discussion,
    69	since both `M·δ + g` and `a·δ + g` exceed `g` for `δ ≥ 1`.
    70	
    71	**RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (I-0660).**  This paragraph continued: `mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound`
    72	"takes `b_L` in exactly the shape `exists_bound_subsingleton_hModule_one_of_isFinite_toP1`
    73	produces it, and *derives* the `m` — so what remains of step 3 is instantiating DAT-0a at the
    74	base-changed curve, not choosing anything."  That is FALSE.  At a chart index legal at parameter

    77	`mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound` itself and `Picard/Pic0ChartCoverageIndexSlack.lean` for the

   196	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   197	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
   198	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
   199	    (b : ℤ)
   200	    (hb : ∀ D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
   201	      b ≤ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D →
   202	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) 1))
   203	    (hdeg : classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
   204	      (chartTwistClass C m Z)) = b) :
   205	    t ∈ chartLocus C m Z lam := by
   206	  -- The instance pack of `BaseChangeInstances` is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling
   207	  -- `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`, not to the `relCurve` alias, so the `relCurve`-spelled
   208	  -- binders of `exists_picClass_eq` / `classDeg_picClass` do not synthesise without these
   209	  -- re-keyings (the same pack `Pic0ChartCoverageFibre.lean:130` needs).  The `hdeg`/`M₀`
   210	  -- binders are therefore stated in the PRODUCT spelling, so that the statement itself needs
   211	  -- no re-keying — `relCurveMap C k L` is `(C ◁ overSpecMap (ofId k L)).left`
   212	  -- (`relCurveMap_eq_overSpecMap_ofId`), which is also the spelling
   213	  -- `classDeg_presenting_twist` delivers.
   214	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C L) := instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   215	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   216	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   217	  haveI : QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
   218	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   219	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   220	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   221	  haveI : Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   222	    instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   223	  obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := Scheme.CurveDivisor.exists_picClass_eq L
   224	    (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L) (chartTwistClass C m Z))
   225	  refine mem_chartLocus_of_witness_h1 C lam t m Z M₀ hM₀ W hW (hb W ?_)
   226	  rw [show Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L W
   227	      = classDeg L (Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass L W) from (classDeg_picClass L W).symm,
   228	    hW, hdeg]
   229	
   230	variable (C) in
   231	/-- **The coverage statement in `∃`-form**, i.e. `w4-datb` §1.2's target shape at a fixed chart
   232	index: at a point whose splitting is known and whose twisted class hits the threshold, there is
   233	a chart the point belongs to.
   234	
   235	Trivial given the previous theorem; recorded because it is the shape the DAT-B B-6 packaging
   236	(`IsLocallySurjective`) consumes, and because keeping it separate makes visible that the only
   237	`∃` coverage still owes is over the *index*, not over any witness or drop. -/
   238	theorem exists_mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (lam : picEt C T)
   239	    (t : T.left) (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   240	    {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra (Over.testPointField t) L]
   241	    [IsScalarTower k (Over.testPointField t) L]
   242	    [Module.Finite (Over.testPointField t) L]
   243	    [Algebra.IsSeparable (Over.testPointField t) L]
   244	    (M₀ : (relCurve C L).CechPic)
   245	    (hM₀ : PicEtAff.map C L
   246	        (picEtAffineEquiv C (Over.testPointField t) (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) lam))
   247	      = PicEtAff.unit C L (relPicMk C (overSpec k L) M₀))
   248	    -- The `classDeg L` of `hdeg` is applied to a `relCurve`-spelled class, and the
   249	    -- `BaseChangeInstances` pack is keyed to the PRODUCT spelling `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left`,
   250	    -- so these three do not synthesise in the STATEMENT (a `haveI` in the proof is too late).
   251	    -- They are not new assumptions: `instIsIntegralBaseChange`,
   252	    -- `instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange` and `instQuasiCompactBaseChange` discharge
   253	    -- them at every instantiation, and the proof below re-derives the rest of the pack.
   254	    [IsIntegral (relCurve C L)]
   255	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   256	    [QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of L))]
   257	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0)]
   258	    [Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1)]
   259	    (b : ℤ)
   260	    (hb : ∀ D : ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left).CurveDivisor,
   261	      b ≤ Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg L D →
   262	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule ((C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.divisorSheaf L D) 1))
   263	    (hdeg : classDeg L (M₀ * Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C k L)
   264	      (chartTwistClass C m Z)) = b) :
   265	    ∃ m' : ℕ, ∃ Z' : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor, t ∈ chartLocus C m' Z' lam :=
   266	  ⟨m, Z, mem_chartLocus_of_vanishing_bound C lam t m Z M₀ hM₀ b hb hdeg⟩
   267

    16	/-!
    17	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that
    35	the evaluation counit sends the canonical unit-lift back to that same section.
    36	-/

    39	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3

    56	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    57	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

    59	/-- A rank-one presentation of a genus-degree plus class on an affine test.
    60	
    61	The two equality fields prevent an unrelated cocycle datum or line bundle from serving as a
    62	witness: `representative` presents the input plus class, `datum_class` presents that same
    63	relative Picard class, and `module_iso` identifies the resulting cocycle sheaf with the
    64	underlying base-ring sheaf of `module`. -/
    65	structure PicRankOneLocalPresentation
    66	    (lam : picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) (overSpec k A)) : Type (u + 1) where
    67	  cover : Algebra.EtaleCover A
    68	  representative : descentClasses C cover
    69	  represents :
    70	    PicEtAff.mk C cover representative = picEtAffineEquiv C A lam.1
    71	  datum : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C cover.Carrier pi
    72	  datum_class :
    73	    (representative : relPic C (overSpec k cover.Carrier)) =
    74	      relPicMk C (overSpec k cover.Carrier) datum.cechPicClass
    75	  module : (relCurve C cover.Carrier).Modules
    76	  module_iso :
    77	    Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
    78	      (Over.mk (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier))) module ≅ datum.sheaf
    79	  line_bundle : Scheme.Modules.IsLineBundle module
    80	  native_pushforward_base_change :
    81	    ∀ {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
    82	      (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
    83	      (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C cover.Carrier)
    84	      (sq : IsPullback g' f'
    85	        (relCurve C cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of cover.Carrier)) g),
    86	      IsIso ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app module)
    87	  h1_vanishing : Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 1)
    88	  h0_finite : Module.Finite cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    89	  h0_projective : Module.Projective cover.Carrier (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0)
    90	  h0_rank_one :
    91	    ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum cover.Carrier,
    92	      Module.rankAtStalk (Sheaf.HModule datum.sheaf 0) p = 1

   104	/-- The canonical `H^0` base-change equivalence attached to a rank-one presentation.

   106	This is derived from `P.h1_vanishing`; it is not an independently chosen witness. -/
   107	noncomputable def h0BaseChange (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   108	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]

   115	/-- The canonical evaluation map attached to a tied local rank-one presentation. -/
   116	noncomputable def evaluation (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :

   118	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj

   120	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ⟶

   127	/-- The canonical native pushforward base-change isomorphism supplied by the presentation.
   128	
   129	The isomorphism is not chosen independently: its hom is definitionally
   130	`(canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.module`. -/
   131	noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIso (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   132	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
   133	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
   134	    (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
   135	    (sq : IsPullback g' f'
   136	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) g) :
   137	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj
   138	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   139	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅
   140	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f').obj ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj P.module) := by
   141	  exact @asIso _ _ _ _ ((canonicalBaseChangeMap sq).app P.module)
   142	    (P.native_pushforward_base_change g f' g' sq)

   144	/-- The native pushforward base-change isomorphism for an affine coefficient extension. -/
   145	noncomputable def nativeBaseChangeIsoAffine (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   146	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   147	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] :
   148	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
   149	      (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap P.cover.Carrier B)))).obj
   150	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   151	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅
   152	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   153	        (relCurve C B ↘ Spec (.of B))).obj
   154	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B)).obj P.module) :=
   155	  P.nativeBaseChangeIso
   156	    (overSpecMap (k := k) P.cover.Carrier B).left
   157	    (snd C (overSpec k B)).left
   158	    (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier B)
   159	    (Over.isPullback_whiskerLeft C (overSpecMap (k := k) P.cover.Carrier B))

   161	/-- The source of evaluation identifies canonically with the source of evaluation after any
   162	cartesian base change. -/
   163	noncomputable def evaluationSourceBaseChangeIso (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   164	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
   165	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
   166	    (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
   167	    (sq : IsPullback g' f'
   168	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) g) :
   169	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback
   170	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⋙
   171	      Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj
   172	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   173	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅
   174	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f' ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback f').obj
   175	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj P.module) :=
   176	  ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
   177	    Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
   178	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g'
   179	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).symm).app
   180	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   181	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module)).symm) ≪≫
   182	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f').mapIso (P.nativeBaseChangeIso g f' g' sq)

   184	/-- Under the source identification, evaluation after base change is the pullback of the
   185	presentation's original evaluation counit. -/
   186	theorem evaluationSourceBaseChangeIso_hom_evaluation
   187	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   188	    {T' X' : Scheme.{u}}
   189	    (g : T' ⟶ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) (f' : X' ⟶ T')
   190	    (g' : X' ⟶ relCurve C P.cover.Carrier)
   191	    (sq : IsPullback g' f'
   192	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) g) :
   193	    (P.evaluationSourceBaseChangeIso g f' g' sq).hom ≫
   194	        (Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction f').counit.app
   195	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').obj P.module) =
   196	      (Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map P.evaluation := by
   197	  change ((((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp f' g) ≪≫
   198	      Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
   199	      (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g'
   200	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).symm).inv).app

   202	            (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module)) ≫

   208	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).counit.app P.module)

   238	/-- The global datum section represented by a degree-zero cohomology class. -/

   247	glued cocycle sheaf; identifying it with native `Scheme.Modules` global sections is a

   249	noncomputable def datumSectionBaseChange (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   250	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]

   260	/-- H⁰ base change transports the tied datum section to the canonical glued-section map. -/
   261	theorem datumSectionBaseChange_one_tmul (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   262	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   263	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B]
   264	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :

   268	    ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing) y
   269	
   270	/-- The conditional divisor datum cut by a base-changed presentation section.
   271	
   272	The explicit `hsec` hypothesis is the non-vacuous fibrewise nonvanishing input.  It is
   273	converted componentwise to the injectivity required by the fibrewise-regular section
   274	construction; the integral fibre instance is installed from the standing geometrically
   275	irreducible curve hypotheses.

   277	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange
   278	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   279	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   280	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
   281	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   282	    (hsec : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
   283	      (P.datum.baseChange B).sectionsMapTop q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   284	        (P.datumSectionBaseChange B y) ≠ 0) :
   285	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations :=
   286	  let D := P.datum.baseChange B
   287	  let s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤) :=
   288	    P.datumSectionBaseChange B y
   289	  D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s
   290	    (fun j q => by
   291	      letI : IsIntegral (relCurve C q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   292	        instIsIntegralBaseChange C q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   293	      exact D.injective_rTensor_component_of_sectionsMapTop_ne_zero s q (hsec q) j)

   295	/-- The conditional section construction preserves the base-changed datum's Picard class. -/
   296	theorem sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange_picClass
   297	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   298	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier B]
   299	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier B] [IsNoetherianRing B]
   300	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   301	    (hsec : ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum B,
   302	      (P.datum.baseChange B).sectionsMapTop q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   303	        (P.datumSectionBaseChange B y) ≠ 0) :
   304	    (P.sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange B y hsec).picClass =
   305	      (P.datum.baseChange B).cechPicClass := by
   306	  let D := P.datum.baseChange B
   307	  let s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤) :=
   308	    P.datumSectionBaseChange B y
   309	  unfold sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange
   310	  exact D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass s
   311	    (fun j q => by
   312	      letI : IsIntegral (relCurve C q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   313	        instIsIntegralBaseChange C q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   314	      exact D.injective_rTensor_component_of_sectionsMapTop_ne_zero s q (hsec q) j)
   315	
   316	/-- The presentation identifies datum `H^0` with native global sections of its line bundle. -/
   317	noncomputable def moduleSectionsEquiv (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam) :
   318	    Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ≃ₗ[P.cover.Carrier] Γ(P.module, ⊤) :=
   319	  (Sheaf.HModule.mapEquiv P.module_iso.symm 0).trans
   320	    (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
   321	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   322	      isTerminalTop
   323	      (Scheme.toModuleKSheafOfModules
   324	        (Over.mk (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))) P.module))
   325	
   326	/-- The native section is exactly the datum section transported through `module_iso`. -/
   327	theorem module_iso_inv_datumSection (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   328	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   329	    (P.module_iso.inv.hom.app (op (⊤ : (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier).Opens))).hom
   330	      (P.datumSection y) = P.moduleSectionsEquiv y := by
   331	  exact Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀_naturality
   332	    (hT := isTerminalTop) (f := P.module_iso.inv) y
   333	
   334	/-- A datum `H^0` class, read as a global section of the native pushforward. -/
   335	noncomputable def pushforwardSectionOfH0 (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   336	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   337	    Γ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   338	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module, ⊤) := by
   339	  change Γ(P.module,
   340	    (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   341	      (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))
   342	  simpa using P.moduleSectionsEquiv y
   343	
   344	/-- The canonical unit-lift of a datum `H^0` class to the source of evaluation. -/
   345	noncomputable def evaluationLiftOfH0 (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   346	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   347	    Γ((Scheme.Modules.pullback
   348	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj
   349	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   350	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module),
   351	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   352	        (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens)) :=
   353	  ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   354	    (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).unit.app
   355	      ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   356	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module)).app
   357	          (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens) (P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y)
   358	
   359	/-- Evaluation of the canonical unit-lift returns the original native global section.
   360	
   361	This is the right triangle identity of pullback-pushforward.  It is the counit compatibility
   362	needed before the section can be used to define a divisor; no zero-locus claim is made here. -/
   363	theorem evaluation_evaluationLiftOfH0 (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   364	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0) :
   365	    (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app P.evaluation
   366	      ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   367	        (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))).hom
   368	      (P.evaluationLiftOfH0 y) = P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y := by
   369	  have h := congrArg
   370	    (fun (f : (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   371	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module ⟶
   372	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   373	        (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) =>
   374	      (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app f (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens)).hom
   375	        (P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y))
   376	    ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction
   377	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).right_triangle_components
   378	        P.module)
   379	  exact h
